**What we’re doing:** Add Google Analytics 4 (GA4) tracking to your Next.js site on Vercel.  
**Who uses it:** Anyone visiting your site (no logins or personal data).  
**Risk level:** **Green** – no sensitive data, no payments, only passive visitor tracking.  

---

### 1️⃣ Quick one‑screen plan  
| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
|GA script | Add the GA4 tag in the `<Head>` of `pages/_document.js` (so it loads on every page). |
|Environment variable | Store the measurement ID in `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`. |
|Vercel secret | Add that env var via the Vercel dashboard (or `.env.local` locally). |
|Deployment | Push the change – Vercel will rebuild and deploy automatically. |
|Verification | Use the browser console or the GA Debugger Chrome extension to confirm hits. |

**Do you have the GA4 Measurement ID?**  
If not, you need to create a GA account at [analytics.google.com](https://analytics.google.com/) and get an ID that looks like `G-XXXXXXX`.  

---

### 2️⃣ Step‑by‑step code changes  

**1. Add the env variable**  
Create or edit `./.env.local` (never commit it – it’s listed in `.gitignore`).  
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID=G-XXXXXXXXX
```
Replace `G-XXXXXXXXX` with your real ID.  

**2. Update the Document**  
Open `pages/_document.js` (create it if it doesn’t exist). Replace content with:

```js
// pages/_document.js
import Document, { Html, Head, Main, NextScript } from 'next/document';

class MyDocument extends Document {
  render() {
    return (
      <Html>
        <Head>
          {/* GA4: Global Site Tag (gtag.js) */}
          <script
            async
            src={`https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID}`}
          />
          <script
            dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
              __html: `
               window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
               function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
               gtag('js', new Date());
               gtag('config', '${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID}');
             `,
            }}
          />
        </Head>
        <body>
          <Main />
          <NextScript />
        </body>
      </Html>
    );
  }
}

export default MyDocument;
```

> **Why this works**  
> The GA tag lives in the `<Head>`, so it’s loaded on every page client‑side.  
> `NEXT_PUBLIC_` makes the variable available in the browser, but it’s still **not** a secret – the measurement ID can be public.

**3. Commit & push**  
```bash
git add .env.local pages/_document.js
git commit -m "Add GA4 tracking"
git push
```
Vercel will rebuild and deploy automatically.  

**4. Verify**  
After deployment:  
- Open the site in Chrome.  
- Press F12 → Console.  
- Look for `gtag('config', 'G-XXXXXXX');`—you should see it fire on each page load.  
- (Optional) Install the **GA Debugger** Chrome extension and enable it to see hits in real time.

---

### 3️⃣ Safety & best practice notes

| Point | Why it matters |
|-------|----------------|
| **Public measurement ID** | GA measurement IDs are meant to be public; no risk. |
| **No secret keys exposed** | All sensitive keys stay on Google’s side. |
| **Third‑party script** | Next.js loads the `gtag.js` script from Google’s CDN, no own server logic. |
| **Backup** | Your changes are in Git – you can roll back if the GA tag breaks something. |

---

### 4️⃣ Next steps

- If you don’t already have a GA account, set one up at analytics.google.com and grab the Measurement ID.  
- Push the changes above.  
- After a few days, check your GA dashboard for traffic data.  

Let me know once you have the Measurement ID or if you hit any snags during these steps!
